'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a male NPC Professor wearing a Synchronist uniform, giving lessons about a catastrophe that caused the [[Solaris-3|Solaris]] axial tilt to shift near the [[Tactical Hologram: Synchronization]] pod during the day.

This axis tilt is the reason for the existence of Roya Frostlands, which was known as the First Epoch by the Royan's<ref>[["A Study of Royan Mythology" (Excerpt)]]</ref><ref>[[Ivar]]</ref>. 

==Location==

{{Dialogue Start}}
==Idle==
:'''Farid:'''  Solaris once experienced a catastrophic shift of both its axis and its magnetic poles.

==Dialogue==
:'''Farid:'''  Alright everyone, our analysis of the ice-core samples from the Roya Frostlands has given us some crucial data—
:'''Farid:'''  It supports a daring hypothesis: Solaris once experienced a catastrophic shift of both its axis and its magnetic poles.
:'''Farid:'''  Think about the force required to shake an entire planet in an instant, far beyond just tectonic activity. 
:{{DIcon}} ...Only a global [[The Lament|Lament]] could cause that.
:'''Farid:'''  Exactly. Ah, you're a freshman from Rabelle College, aren't you? Sharp insight.
:{{DIcon}} I'm flattered. Just following your reasoning, Professor.
:'''Farid:'''  ...Very well. Moving on.
:'''Farid:'''  In the aftermath, the [[Etheric Sea]] spread, engulfing Solaris and completely transforming its ecology.
:'''Farid:'''  The cascade of effects that followed triggered the largest mass extinction in recorded history.
:'''Farid:'''  We even suspect the Etheric Sea didn't just physically separate Solaris from the rest of the universe. It may have isolated its very laws.
:'''Farid:'''  Could the new order reshaping Solaris have originated from that mysterious floating sea itself?
:{{DIcon}} ...So you're saying Solaris's physics just stopped working?
:'''Farid:'''  Hehe, that's a bit of academic hyperbole. The laws of physics still exist, there are just far too many new variables for our models to handle.
:'''Farid:'''  Anyway, the key to all of this likely lies where the planet's axis and magnetic poles now converge.
:'''Farid:'''  It's the leading theory in the field right now.
{{Dialogue End}}
